commits.pr_title: [BugFix][DiffusionGemma][CPU] Copy async output snapshots instead of aliasing reused buffers
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #59828

## Claims

With async scheduling, the V2 model runner snapshots each step's sampled tokens and counts with `async_copy_to_np()`. It reads them after the next step starts. On GPU, `.to("cpu")` copies into new memory. On CPU it returns the same tensor, and the snapshot aliases the sampler's buffers. DiffusionGemma reuses those buffers on every step, and the next step overwrites the snapshot before it is read.

This is latent on `main`. CPU forces sync scheduling, which reads each output before the next step runs. I found it while testing DiffusionGemma structured reads on CPU with async scheduling enabled, after https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59107. Every read returned a phantom first token, overwritten tokens and one logprob row too few.

### Changes in this PR

- `async_copy_to_np()` passes `copy=True`. A CPU snapshot now owns its memory. GPU behavior does not change. The device-to-host copy already allocates.
- Add a regression test to `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py`, next to the other V2 model runner tests, instead of a new file. It snapshots a CPU tensor, overwrites the tensor and checks that the snapshot keeps its values.

I checked the other snapshots in `AsyncOutput`. Logprobs, sampling masks and prompt logprobs also alias on CPU. They are safe because their producers allocate new tensors on every step. I left them as is.

No open issue or PR covers this. I searched for `async_copy_to_np`, CPU async aliasing and overwritten sampled tokens. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58082 edits the code next to `async_copy_to_np()` but does not change it.

I used Claude Code to help with this PR. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests below.

## Validation

Hardware: 22 vCPU Intel Xeon Platinum 8481C, Ubuntu 22.04, PyTorch 2.13.0+cpu. vLLM built from source for CPU at e006d761a5, with the real `google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it` checkpoint in BF16. Unit tests also on macOS (Apple Silicon).

**Unit tests:**

```bash
pytest -v tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py
```

**End to end:**

1. Sync path, the default on CPU. Run greedy generation with `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` and a DiffusionGemma structured read (32-token canvas on a 64-token server). Run on `main`, with this PR, and on `main` again for the noise floor. Compare tokens, logprobs and throughput.
2. Async path. Enable async scheduling on CPU with a local change to `CpuPlatform.check_and_update_config()`. Send the same DiffusionGemma read 10 times with a batch of 1 and 10 times with a batch of 4. Compare each read with sync.

## Test Result

Before (`main`, async on CPU), the read's tokens are overwritten. The issue has the details and the `collect_env.py` output.

```text
sync   tokens[:8] [45518, 45518, 107, 148436, 148436, 236787, 11262, 1]   logprob rows 32
async  tokens[:8] [45518, 1, 1, 1, 1, 148436, 236787, 11262]              logprob rows 31
```

After:

- Unit tests: 90 passed. The new test fails on `main` with `assert [1, 1, 1, 1] == [0, 0, 0, 0]`.
- Async: 50/50 reads match sync, up from 0/50. No snapshot changes before it is read, even with the reader delayed by 50 ms.
- Sync: [layer 3 results: tokens and logprobs before and after for both models, throughput against the noise floor]

## Details

On CPU, .to("cpu") returns the same tensor, and with async scheduling the next step overwrites the sampled-token snapshot before it is read. That corrupted every DiffusionGemma read I tested (linked in the issue).

This PR copies in `async_copy_to_np()`, the one place sampler outputs cross the async boundary. GPU behavior does not change. CPU pays one small copy per step. main is unaffected today because CPU forces sync scheduling. Logprob snapshots still alias but stay safe because their producers allocate new tensors.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Validate incompatible MoE adapter formats
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Reject fused 3D MoE LoRA weights on a 2D wrapper when the required format settings are missing, with an error naming both settings.

Addresses the actionable-error follow-up in item 4 of #59799; complements #59801.

## Claims

- Detect this incompatible layout before adapter registration and activation.
- Explain how to enable `enable_mixed_moe_lora_format` and set `is_3d_lora_weight`.
- Check during worker loading before replacing or evicting a cached adapter.

## Validation

Validated on one NVIDIA A10G (AWS g5.2xlarge), FP16, using a tiny random Qwen3-MoE model and a PEFT 0.21.2 adapter, based on commit `6f75cc7d5d1b5adfb399cbf79a8231ae66844fcf`.

These results cover the patch committed as `2f8c900063f3`, before the subsequent merge of `main` into this branch. They are not CI results for the updated PR head.

- `python -m pytest tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py -v`: **28 passed**, including eight new cases.
- `pre-commit run --files vllm/lora/model_manager.py vllm/lora/worker_manager.py tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py docs/features/lora.md`: all applicable hooks passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

| Full-engine case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Original reproducer, missing both settings | Bare assertion replaced by a descriptive worker `ValueError`; generation still ends with `EngineDeadError`. |
| Original reproducer, both settings enabled | Generates `[190, 737, 34, 78]`, matching the baseline control. |
| Dynamic `add_lora`, each of the three missing-flag combinations | Returns the actionable error; generation continues afterward. |
| Dynamic rejection with a valid adapter already filling the cache | Valid adapter ID remains registered; deterministic generation is unchanged. |

The original generation reproducer is in #59799; these runs use FP16 on the
A10G. The dynamic-loading harness below is self-contained:

```sh
VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn python validate_59799.py
VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn python validate_59799.py --mixed
```

Both commands complete successfully. New unit cases run in the existing LoRA CI
job. Multi-GPU behavior and HTTP serving were not tested.

This is a loading/activation smoke test, not a model-quality evaluation. The change does not alter LoRA scaling, conversion or kernels.

<details>
<summary>Dynamic-loading validation harness (save as validate_59799.py)</summary>

```python
"""Validate dynamic loading errors and continued generation on a CUDA engine."""
import argparse
from pathlib import Path
import tempfile
import torch
from peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, Qwen3MoeConfig
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
from vllm.inputs import TokensPrompt
from vllm.lora.request import LoRARequest


def make_checkpoint(directory):
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    config = Qwen3MoeConfig(
        vocab_size=1024, hidden_size=256, intermediate_size=512,
        moe_intermediate_size=128, num_hidden_layers=2,
        num_attention_heads=4, num_key_value_heads=2, head_dim=64,
        num_experts=8, num_experts_per_tok=2, tie_word_embeddings=False,
    )
    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_config(config, dtype=torch.float16)
    model.save_pretrained(directory / "base")
    lora = LoraConfig(
        r=16, lora_alpha=32, target_modules=[],
        target_parameters=["mlp.experts.gate_up_proj", "mlp.experts.down_proj"],
    )
    get_peft_model(model, lora).save_pretrained(directory / "lora")

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--mixed", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        directory = Path(tmp)
        make_checkpoint(directory)
        llm = LLM(str(directory / "base"), skip_tokenizer_init=True,
                  dtype="float16", enable_lora=True, max_lora_rank=16,
                  max_cpu_loras=1, max_loras=1, max_model_len=256,
                  gpu_memory_utilization=0.3, enforce_eager=True,
                  enable_mixed_moe_lora_format=args.mixed)
        prompt = TokensPrompt(prompt_token_ids=list(range(10, 40)))
        params = SamplingParams(max_tokens=4, temperature=0, detokenize=False)
        engine = llm.llm_engine
        good = LoRARequest("good", 1, str(directory / "lora"), is_3d_lora_weight=True)
        if args.mixed:
            assert engine.add_lora(good)
            before = llm.generate(prompt, params, lora_request=good)[0].outputs[0].token_ids
            expected_ids = {1}
        else:
            before = llm.generate(prompt, params)[0].outputs[0].token_ids
            expected_ids = set()
        declarations = [False] if args.mixed else [False, True]
        for declared in declarations:
            bad = LoRARequest("bad", 2, str(directory / "lora"), is_3d_lora_weight=declared)
            try:
                engine.add_lora(bad)
            except Exception as exc:
                message = str(exc)
                assert "enable_mixed_moe_lora_format=True" in message, message
                assert "is_3d_lora_weight=True" in message, message
                print("EXPECTED REJECTION:", type(exc).__name__, message, flush=True)
            else:
                raise AssertionError("Incompatible adapter was accepted")
            actual_ids = engine.list_loras()
            print("REGISTERED ADAPTERS:", repr(actual_ids), flush=True)
            assert set(actual_ids) == expected_ids, actual_ids
            after = llm.generate(prompt, params, lora_request=good if args.mixed else None)[0].outputs[0].token_ids
            assert after == before, (before, after)
            print("PASS: engine remains usable; adapters", expected_ids, "tokens", after, flush=True)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

</details>

## Details

Without both format settings, fused expert tensors reach `FusedMoEWithLoRA.set_lora`, which expects packed lists and raises a bare assertion. The validator checks actual loaded weights and wrapper type, preserving native 3D wrappers and the supported mixed-format conversion path. Per-expert and attention-only adapters are not rejected.

The check runs on adapter loading, not each token. It is deliberately limited to this layout mismatch; it does not provide general adapter validation or change exception handling during generation. Lazy loading through `LLM.generate()` can still terminate the engine, now with actionable configuration guidance in the worker error.

No duplication: #59801 handles per-module scaling and rank validation and explicitly leaves this error-handling follow-up open. #52198 handles tensor orientation, and #59915 handles Inkling-specific conversion.

AI assistance: Codex was used for implementation, regression tests, and GPU validation.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Fix multimodal embedding merge in Llama 4 and Mistral Large 3 EAGLE drafters
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #57630.

Regression from #50417 (first released in v0.28.0): that change marked these drafters as `SupportsMultiModalEmbeddings` so the speculator started routing multimodal batches through their `embed_input_ids`, which had been an unreachable alias of `SupportsMultiModal.embed_input_ids` until then. cc @TQCB

`EagleLlama4ForCausalLM` and `EagleMistralLarge3ForCausalLM` implement `SupportsMultiModalEmbeddings` by borrowing the method object `SupportsMultiModal.embed_input_ids`. That method calls `self._embed_text_input_ids(...)` and reads `self._has_oov_mm_tokens`, both of which live on `SupportsMultiModal`, which the drafters do not inherit. Any multimodal target paired with one of these drafters fails during the first draft prefill (already in the profile run at startup):

```
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/autoregressive/speculator.py", line 427, in _run_model
File "vllm/model_executor/models/interfaces.py", line 507, in embed_input_ids
AttributeError: 'EagleLlama4ForCausalLM' object has no attribute '_embed_text_input_ids'. Did you mean: 'embed_input_ids'?
```

Reproduced on main (bf13ecc) and present in v0.28.0 and v0.29.0 with `RedHatAI/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct-quantized.w4a16` + `morgendave/EAGLE-Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct`, TP=4, `--speculative-config '{"method":"eagle","model":...,"num_speculative_tokens":3}'`, default cudagraph mode. The same aliasing exists in `EagleMistralLarge3ForCausalLM`; Model Runner V1 takes the same `embed_input_ids` path.

## Change

Replace the borrowed method with an explicit `embed_input_ids` in both drafters that embeds the draft input ids via `self.model.embed_input_ids` and merges external multimodal embeddings with `_merge_multimodal_embeddings`, the same shape `EagleMistralForCausalLM` already uses. No behavior change for text-only batches.

## Test plan

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_autoregressive_speculator.py -v   # 21 passed (2 new)
pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/models/llama4_eagle.py vllm/model_executor/models/mistral_large_3_eagle.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_autoregressive_speculator.py
```

New test `test_mm_capable_drafter_merges_multimodal_embeddings` (parametrized over both classes) checks text-only embedding and the merge of multimodal rows; it raises `AttributeError` on main.

E2E (4x NVIDIA L4, TP=4, TRITON_ATTN, `RedHatAI/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct-quantized.w4a16` + `morgendave/EAGLE-Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct`, `num_speculative_tokens=3`, `max_patches=4`, 18 text + 12 image prompts, greedy, 48 new tokens):

| build | cudagraph_mode | text AL | image AL | image per-pos acceptance |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main @ bf13ecc | FULL_AND_PIECEWISE | startup crash (`AttributeError: ... '_embed_text_input_ids'`) | | |
| main + this PR | FULL_AND_PIECEWISE | 2.637 (328 drafts) | 2.424 (238 drafts) | 0.710 / 0.445 / 0.269 |
| main + this PR | NONE | 2.674 (322 drafts) | 2.413 (240 drafts) | 0.708 / 0.446 / 0.258 |

Image prompts now draft with acceptance close to text prompts, i.e. the drafter is receiving the image embeddings.

## Disclosure

AI assistance (Claude) was used to investigate and draft this change; every line was reviewed and the tests were run by the submitter.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][EC Connector] Release shared memory on NIXL setup failure
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Prevent leaked shared memory when ECCPU scheduler initialization fails with NIXL enabled. The constructor currently raises without releasing the region it has already allocated.

## Claims

- Failed NIXL setup releases the scheduler-owned mmap file, file descriptors, and mapping while preserving the original exception.

## Validation

Review validation with NIXL 1.4.1: the previous constructor test file reproduced the test-order failure (6 passed, 1 failed); importing `data.nixl` before monkeypatching fixes its cached bindings, and all 7 constructor tests pass together. The suites below were rerun after merging upstream main.

The missing-NIXL regression fails against the unchanged scheduler because the mmap file remains, and passes with this fix. A second CPU regression raises during control-transport creation after data transport setup, and checks deregistration, shared-region release, and preservation of the original exception.

```bash
uv run --no-project --python .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_scheduler_nixl_ctor.py \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/cpu/scheduler \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/cpu/test_ec_shared_region.py -q
# 76 passed (NIXL 1.4.1 installed)

uv run --no-project --python .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  -m cpu_test tests/v1/ec_connector/unit -q
# 62 passed, 350 deselected

uv run --no-project --python .venv/bin/python pre-commit run --files \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_scheduler_nixl_ctor.py \
  vllm/distributed/ec_transfer/ec_connector/cpu/scheduler/__init__.py
# All applicable hooks passed, including mypy and test tethering.
```


Nearby transport/session/scheduler tests also passed (95 tests):

```bash
uv run --no-project --python .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_data.py \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_session.py \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_control.py \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_scheduler_nixl_consumer.py \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_scheduler_nixl_producer.py -q
```

A separate CPU check exercised `ECConnectorFactory` through `ECCPUConnector` using real `VllmConfig`/`ModelConfig` objects and a local tiny Llava configuration, without replacing the shared-memory factory. The unchanged scheduler left the file, two file descriptors, and a mapping after the missing-NIXL error; the fixed scheduler left none, with the same error. Descriptors and mappings were checked through `/proc/self/fd` and `/proc/self/maps`.

Environment: Ubuntu 24.04 under WSL, Python 3.12.14, torch 2.13.0+cpu, editable source with official v0.30.0 CPU precompiled binaries. Exact-commit CPU binaries were unavailable. NIXL 1.4.1 was installed for this review revision, and the constructor wiring test exercised real NIXL registration and ZMQ session startup. Full GPU serving and cross-process NIXL data transfer were not run; local validation covers scheduler construction and startup-failure cleanup. The new test is selected by the existing CPU EC connector job in `.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml`.

## Details

The region is allocated before `_setup_nixl`; if setup raises, the caller never receives a scheduler to shut down. The constructor owns failure unwinding through `shutdown()`, releasing NIXL resources before the shared region. `_setup_nixl()` propagates errors without a second cleanup handler.

Related: #56507, #56508. The related test/doc PR covers import isolation and documentation, rather than constructor cleanup. Searches for EC scheduler cleanup, NIXL initialization, and shared-memory leaks found no equivalent open PR.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex prepared the patch and this review revision, and ran the validation above. The submitting human reviewed the original patch, personally reran its 74-pass/1-skip suite, and authorized this revision to address the review. No inference-output or performance change is claimed.

Depends on vllm-project/ci-infra#727, which must merge first.

- The GH200 step no longer runs its own `docker build`; it `depends_on: arm64-image-build` and runs in that image.
- `.buildkite/scripts/hardware_ci/run-gh200-test.sh` is deleted.

Not yet run on a GH200 agent. The step is `optional`, so it needs to be unblocked on this PR once vllm-project/ci-infra#727 is in; that run is the validation.

commits.pr_title: [Perf] Reduce fallback decode CPU by 69% at 32K
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fallback detokenization copies the full token-string history on every decode step, even though it reads only the trailing window. This change copies the required window and keeps the caller's absolute offsets.

## Claims

- **69% lower fallback decode CPU time** at 32,768 tokens per request in the final-output replay: **7.46 s → 2.30 s**.
- Decoded text and token IDs match the baseline. Prompt initialization and offset behavior are preserved.

## Validation

The replay runs the real `SlowIncrementalDetokenizer` caller on one CPU core, with four English, Chinese, Burmese, and emoji inputs and the Pixtral Mistral tokenizer. Each version has one warmup and three timed runs per size and output mode. Times cover all four requests. No model inference runs in this benchmark.

| Tokens per request | Output | Baseline CPU median (range) | Patch CPU median (range) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8,192 | Final | 0.85 s (0.83–0.88) | 0.51 s (0.50–0.52) |
| 32,768 | Final | 7.46 s (7.34–7.62) | 2.30 s (2.26–2.33) |
| 32,768 | Streamed | 8.85 s (8.80–9.04) | 2.28 s (2.26–2.36) |

Live checks used Ministral-3-3B-Instruct-2512 on one L4. All 24 baseline/patch response pairs matched text, token IDs, finish and stop reasons, and usage. Four requests of 6,144 tokens showed no confirmed serving gain: request-time medians were 145.03 s and 145.23 s. API CPU medians were 4.64 s and 4.765 s, with overlapping ranges. The 69% claim applies to the replay above.

Tests run on both helper versions:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tokenizers_/test_detokenize.py -q -k '(gpt2 or Pixtral or long_history or prompt_window) and not logprobs_count'
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py -q
```

Each version passed **81 tokenizer tests and 94 renderer tests**. There were 91 existing skips, 660 deselected cases, and one expected failure. The added cases cover long Unicode output, the first-call prompt window, and offsets past the window. The 81 tokenizer tests passed again on both helper versions after the base update. Local pre-commit and Python 3.12 mypy checks passed. Upstream CI is enabled. Its failed steps are being checked and retried.

## Details

`prev_tokens + new_tokens` creates the full-history copy before the helper takes its decode slices. The patch starts at the earliest required offset and adjusts the slice indexes within that window. It returns the full token count as the absolute read offset and keeps the initial prompt tokens. The window can still grow when text is incomplete. Other copies in the caller remain.

This removes a full-history copy in the Python fallback helper. The open prompt-priming PRs #51281 and #57330 change the fast `DecodeStream` path. PR #46723 changes the Rust frontend. These are separate code paths.

<details>
<summary>Benchmark reproduction and test environment</summary>

Use this [benchmark script](https://github.com/spa5k/vllm/blob/4d8b5db4daef6d5ef38332d0d2df57bdff47aa53/benchmarks/benchmark_fallback_detokenizer.py), saved as `/tmp/vllm_fallback_benchmark.py`. Run each command on the base and patch with the same tokenizer cache:

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Keep the GLM-5.3 kpool tail and Qwen4 QSA ring out of the null block
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Block id 0 is the null block. It is shared by every KV cache group and is assumed to stay zero. Since #35431, the runners mark rows that own no state with 0 in the block table, not `PAD_SLOT_ID`: dummy runs, CUDA graph capture and padding rows all carry 0. Two ring caches that address their pages through column 0 of the block table did not treat 0 as "no ring", so dummy runs wrote their rows into block 0:

- **GLM-5.3-Flash kpool tail:** `_kpool_tail_slot_mapping_kernel` maps every token to `block_table[req][0] * kpool + pos % kpool`. Its torch fallback does the same.
- **Qwen4 QSA circular ring:** `circular_qsa_slot_mapping` and `_build_qsa_metadata_kernel` map tokens to `block_table[req, 0]` and kept every block `>= 0`. The compressed QSA path already keeps dummy slots inert (`test_qsa_compressed_metadata_keeps_dummy_slots_inert`); the ring path did not.

Every scheduled request owns its ring block, so a request on the null block has none. Its tokens now map to PAD, as the generic slot mapping does. The ring writers already skip PAD slots.

This is the same pattern as #58560, which fixes the DeepSeek-V4.1 compressor ring.

## Changes

- `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py`: the kpool tail slot mapping (Triton and torch) emits PAD for requests on the null block.
- `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/common/qsa_cache.py`: the QSA circular ring slot mapping (torch and Triton) requires block `> 0`.
- Tests: the existing QSA circular metadata test, which runs the Triton builder, also checks a dummy batch (all-zero block table) and expects PAD. QSA tests that used block 0 as a real ring block now start real blocks at 1. This includes `_make_block_table` in the AMD pre-indexer test, which could randomly hand out block 0. For the kpool tail, the existing CPU padding test now ends with a padding request on the null block, and the existing Triton-vs-CPU test adds a mixed batch and an all-null dummy batch. Both check that the null-block request maps to PAD.

## Not a duplicate

- #58560 covers only the DeepSeek-V4.1 compressor ring.
- #57158 zeroes block 0 after capture. That does not cover DP idle-rank dummy batches during serving.
- #57169 and #59297 move the kpool tail onto `CircularBufferSpec` / the packed layout but keep its slot kernel unchanged.
- #54296 masks out-of-range block indices in the generic slot mapping kernel, which neither ring uses.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_pre_indexer_amd.py tests/v1/attention/test_kpool_tail_slot_mapping.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_kpool_tail_slot_mapping.py
pre-commit run --files <changed files>
```

## Test Result

- Rebased on main `d6fe5dca68`. 102 passed, 16 skipped on GB200. The 16 skips are `test_qsa_pre_indexer_amd.py`, which requires ROCm.
- Control: with the QSA change reverted, the dummy-batch check fails: dummy tokens map to real slots in block 0.
- Control: with the kpool tail change reverted, the CPU padding test and the two null-block Triton cases fail.
- `pre-commit` passes.
- No model eval. Only tokens of requests on the null block change, and those are dummy or padding rows whose outputs are discarded. Real requests never own block 0 (`BlockPool` pops it as the null block at init), so their mappings and outputs are unchanged.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Build] Fail fast when `setup.py develop` deps aren't pip-preinstalled
commits.pr_body:
Recently hit this issue (#34073) myself when installing vLLM in editable mode in a ROCm container. This PR adds a preflight check that fails fast with an actionable error- pointing the user to run `pip install -r requirements/rocm.txt`,  instead of letting `python setup.py develop` crash deep in a C compile step.

## Purpose

`python setup.py develop` on ROCm resolves missing `install_requires` via setuptools' legacy `easy_install` path instead of pip's resolver. That path has repeatedly failed trying to compile old sdists of fast-moving C-extension packages (e.g. `aiohttp`) from source, surfacing as a cryptic compiler error instead of the real dependency problem:

```
aiohttp/_websocket.c:196:12: fatal error: longintrepr.h: No such file or directory
```

Reported in #34073. The [ROCm docs](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/docs/getting_started/installation/gpu.rocm.inc.md) already recommend `pip install -r requirements/rocm.txt` before `python setup.py develop`, but users who skip that step still hit this confusing failure with no indication of the real cause.

## What this changes

Adds `_check_requirements_preinstalled()`, scoped to `_is_hip() and "develop" in sys.argv[1:]`. Before setuptools' resolver runs, it verifies every `requirements/rocm.txt` entry is installed and version-satisfied, raising an actionable error if not:

```
The following dependencies are missing or outdated:
  aiohttp >= 3.14.3

`python setup.py develop` cannot reliably install these itself (see
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/34073). Install them with pip
first, e.g.:
  pip install -r requirements/rocm.txt
then re-run `python setup.py develop`.
```

The check is skipped when `--no-deps` is passed: that flag makes setuptools skip `install_requires` processing entirely, so the failure this guards against can't occur. This also keeps the existing `python_only_compile.sh` ROCm CI job (which runs `setup.py develop --no-deps`) unaffected.

No other build path is touched — `bdist_wheel`, `egg_info`, and pip's isolated builds (used by `docker/Dockerfile.rocm` and CI) don't match this scoping and already install `requirements/rocm.txt` before building.

## Test Plan & Result

- `python3 -m py_compile setup.py`
- Verified all 78 flattened lines in `requirements/rocm.txt` parse via `packaging.requirements.Requirement`.
- Simulated the check against real installed packages: flags missing/outdated requirements, stays silent when satisfied, and no-ops under `--no-deps`.

No functional change for any build path except `python setup.py develop` on ROCm with unmet dependencies, which now fails fast with a clear message instead of a cryptic C compiler error.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][NIXL] Transfer the whole PLE short-conv page in disaggregated P/D
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #59642 (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: 0% MTP acceptance in disaggregated P/D serving with `NixlConnector`).

The NIXL worker folds every KV cache layer that reports the same base address into one region (`register_kv_caches`, `if base_addr in seen_base_addresses`). In the block-outer HMA layout every cache group places its first page at byte 0 of the shared allocation, so on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next the PLE short-conv state (`Qwen4ExpPLELayer`, a tp-replicated `MambaSpec`, page = `channels × (conv_state_len + num_spec_tokens)` = 245760 B) lands in the same region as layer-0 GDN, the layer-3 QSA ring and the layer-3 MLA indexer cache, and that region keeps the MLA page length (204800 B). The PLE descriptors built from `block_len_per_layer[_ple_region_index]` therefore transfer only 204800/245760 bytes of each PLE slot: 8534 of 10240 channels arrive on the decode worker, the rest is whatever the block held before (never zeroed: the block is exempt from zeroing because an async load is expected to overwrite it). With `num_speculative_tokens >= 2` the spec-decode short conv reads those stale columns, the layer-1 hidden state becomes NaN, the target logits are NaN and the rejection sampler rejects every draft (the generated tokens are garbage too, not just slow).

This PR records the PLE page length at registration (`_ple_block_len`) and uses it for the PLE descriptors on both sides of the transfer (`_build_mamba_local` / `_build_mamba_remote`), exchanging it through `NixlAgentMetadata.ple_block_len` (optional, backward compatible) so the existing P/D geometry check still compares PLE pages. Region discovery is unchanged: the PLE keeps sharing its region with the pages it aliases, as `test_csa_linear_registration_discovers_shared_regions` expects; only the transfer length of its pages changes.

## Test Plan

- New unit test `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_ple_region.py`: a CSA-linear-like config (MLA + GDN + ring + PLE sharing byte 0 of one block-outer tensor, PLE page larger than the MLA page); asserts the PLE descriptors cover the whole PLE page and that the page length is advertised in the handshake metadata. Before the fix the PLE descriptors carry the MLA page length.
- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py` + `test_nixl_desc_geometry.py` run inside the serving image (vLLM `109b5363fc`) with the patch hot-patched: 307 passed before and after (one HF-download test deselected).
- End-to-end on GB200 (vLLM `109b5363fc` + this patch hot-patched into the image, Dynamo + `NixlConnector`, 1P/1D, `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4`, MTP k=3, 200 requests of 64/64 tokens): mean acceptance length goes from 1.00 on 20/21 windows (zero accepted drafts) to 2.7–3.5 on every window, no NaN; the same configuration in aggregate mode gives ~2.1–2.4.

## Test Result

See above; details and the full investigation (per-request probes of the PLE conv state on prefill and decode, per-column comparison of the transferred slot) are in #59642.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Route by swap-row capacity, not the index-group workspace
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

HiSparse crashes when a batch has exactly `max_num_seqs * max_decode_query_len + 1` tokens. With `max_num_seqs=1` the engine fails at startup, and with `max_num_seqs=2` a 3-token prompt crashes at runtime:

```
ValueError: HiSparse swap rows exceed the configured speculative decode capacity: stop=2, capacity=1.
```

Part of #60072.

## Claims

- HiSparse now routes a batch to `swap_in` only when the batch fits the swap rows that `swap_in` consumes. Larger batches take the existing all-resident fallback.
- No performance impact: the change is a Python-side routing comparison against a fixed size. Batches up to the swap capacity take the same path as before; only the single size that crashed changes path.

## Validation

1×H200, upstream `main` 242e4213fc. Repro (tiny DeepSeek-V3.2, dummy weights):

```python
import sys
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
from vllm.config import AttentionConfig, HiSparseConfig, KVTransferConfig

llm = LLM(
    "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2", load_format="dummy",
    hf_overrides={"num_hidden_layers": 8, "hidden_size": 256, "intermediate_size": 512,
                  "num_attention_heads": 8, "num_key_value_heads": 1, "n_routed_experts": 8,
                  "num_experts_per_tok": 2, "index_topk": 128},
    max_model_len=320, block_size=64, max_num_seqs=int(sys.argv[1]),
    enable_prefix_caching=False, gpu_memory_utilization=0.3,
    kv_transfer_config=KVTransferConfig(kv_connector="HiSparseConnector", kv_role="kv_both",
                                        kv_connector_extra_config={"host_pool_gib": 1}),
    attention_config=AttentionConfig(hisparse_config=HiSparseConfig()),
)
for n in (2, 3, 200):
    llm.generate([{"prompt_token_ids": list(range(100, 100 + n))}],
                 SamplingParams(max_tokens=8, ignore_eos=True))
```

| Command | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `python repro.py 1` | Startup fails during piecewise CUDA-graph capture at size 2: `stop=2, capacity=1` | All 3 prompts complete |
| `python repro.py 2` | Startup succeeds; the 3-token prompt crashes: `stop=3, capacity=2` | All 3 prompts complete |
| 61-layer DeepSeek-V3.2 (8 experts, dummy weights), `max_num_seqs=1`, 16k context, 256 output tokens, `host_pool_gib=32` | Startup fails: `stop=2, capacity=1` | Runs; TPOT 18.4 ms over 3 reps |

Tests on this PR (each command run separately):

- `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k "hisparse or index_group"`: 40 passed. The regression case `test_hisparse_resident_prefill_uses_attention_block_stride` fails on `main` and passes with this PR.
- `pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py`: 9 passed
- `pytest tests/v1/core -k hisparse`: 72 passed
- `pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py`: 4 passed

## Details

**Root cause.** `HiSparseMLAIndexGroup.convert_logical_to_physical_topk` sends a batch to `swap_in` whenever the batch fits `physical_topk_indices`. That index-group workspace is allocated with one spare row (`max_decode_rows + 1`). `swap_in`, however, writes into the HiSparse runtime's shared swap rows, which hold exactly `min(max_num_batched_tokens, max_num_seqs * max_decode_query_len)` rows. A batch one token larger than the swap capacity therefore passes the routing check and then overflows in `_step_rows`.

With `max_num_seqs=1`, the CUDA-graph capture sizes are `[1, 2]`. The 2-token piecewise capture follows the all-resident prefill path into this conversion, so the engine fails at startup. With `max_num_seqs=2`, capture sizes `[1, 2, 4]` skip 3 tokens, so the failure only appears when a real 3-token batch arrives.

**Fix.** Route on `HiSparseRuntime.max_swap_rows`, the capacity that `swap_in` actually consumes. The non-HiSparse `SparseMLAIndexGroup` does not change.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Structured Output] Feed the token that implicitly ends reasoning to the grammar
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Structured output skipped a reasoning-end token that is also content, such as GLM's `<tool_call>` with no `</think>` before it. The grammar then forced a second `<tool_call>`, and `required`/named tool calls were lost. This PR feeds that token to the grammar, which matches what `extract_content_ids` already does. Fixes #59608.

## Claims

- For `ParserEngine`-based parsers, the grammar now consumes a reasoning-end token that `extract_content_ids` keeps as content, if the grammar accepts it. Close tags such as `</think>` are still skipped. `ReasoningParser` and legacy parsers do not change.
- On GLM-5.3-Flash, the doubled-`<tool_call>` signature went from 7/40 (`required`) and 8/40 (named) to 0/40. With MTP speculative decoding it went from 9/40 and 11/40 to 0/40.
- Under speculative decoding, a drafted `<tool_call>` cannot force the end of reasoning, and when it is the last draft the bonus row is masked from the grammar state after it.
- The same failure reproduces on Qwen3 (`qwen3` + `hermes`), and the fix removes it there too. Correct-call rates on the GLM tool-result prompt did not go up, because of a separate argument bug (see Limitations).

## Validation

### Unit tests

```
pytest tests/v1/structured_output tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp_structured_output.py tests/parser \
  tests/reasoning tests/tool_parsers/test_glm47_moe_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_glm4_moe_tool_parser.py \
  --ignore=tests/parser/cohere
```

Result with 1 GPU visible: 6402 passed, 1 xfailed. `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` and the manual mypy-3.12 hook pass.

New tests are `test_inclusive_reasoning_end_token` and `test_end_token_committed_alone` in `tests/v1/structured_output/test_structured_output_manager.py` (xgrammar and guidance), and `test_implicit_reasoning_end_of_parsers` (real `glm47_moe` config) in `tests/parser/engine/test_parser_engine.py`. With grammar start forced to the constraint start, 8 of the 13 new cases fail: `inclusive`, `inclusive_first`, `inclusive_last` and `no_drafts`, on both backends.

CI runs these tests through `misc.yaml`. `tests/parser/cohere` is left out because it needs the optional `cohere_melody` package.

A CPU script that drives the scheduler flow (validate drafts, bitmask, accept, next bitmask) with `<tool_call>` as the last draft, the only draft, a mid-window draft and the recovered token gives a second `<tool_call>` in all 8 stock cases and none with the fix.

### Live runs

The live runs used the first version of this PR (5805e42cfa). The current commit only restructures that code, and the unit tests and the CPU check give the same results on both versions.

GLM-5.3-Flash (`RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4`), TP4 on H100, xgrammar, the tool-result repro from the issue, 40 seeds at temperature 0.7:

```
vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --max-model-len 32768 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  [--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}']
```

| Doubled-`<tool_call>` signatures, 40 seeds | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `required` | 7 | **0** |
| named | 8 | **0** |
| `required`, MTP | 9 | **0** |
| named, MTP | 11 | **0** |

MTP draft acceptance was 59.1% before and 58.5% after.

Qwen3 (`Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, `--tool-call-parser hermes --reasoning-parser qwen3`), `logit_bias` -100 on `</think>` and +5 on `<tool_call>`, temperature 0, 3 repeats:

```
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.5 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes --reasoning-parser qwen3
```

| Mode | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `required` | 0/3 calls, 3/3 signatures | **3/3 calls** |
| named | 0/3 calls, 3/3 signatures | **3/3 calls** |
| `auto` (control) | 3/3 calls | 3/3 calls |

No standard tool-calling eval (such as BFCL) was run.

## Details

**Root cause.** `_get_constraint_start` returned the index after the reasoning-end token. That is right for `</think>`, which is not content. A tool-call start that ends reasoning is content, so the grammar started one token after the content did. This came in with #55223, and #48200 kept it.

**Change.**

- `ParserEngine.find_reasoning_end_offset` becomes `find_reasoning_end`, which returns `ReasoningEnd(offset, implicit)`. `implicit` is True when the end token is not the close tag, the same rule `extract_content_ids` uses.
- `StructuredOutputManager._get_constraint_start` becomes `_get_constraint_bounds`, which returns `ConstraintBounds(grammar_start, constraint_start)`. For an implicit end that the grammar accepts, the grammar starts at the end token and masking starts one token later. Otherwise both equal the old value.
- `validate_tokens`, the spec-decode loop of `grammar_bitmask` and `accept_tokens` feed the grammar from `grammar_start`. Masked rows and early returns still use `constraint_start`, so a drafted `<tool_call>` cannot force the target to end reasoning.
- The "grammar accepts it" check keeps the old skip when the grammar cannot start with that token, such as a `json_schema` response format with tools present.

**Affected parsers.** Every in-tree `ParserEngine` config whose tool-call start ends reasoning now feeds that token to the grammar: glm47_moe (and ling3), qwen3 (and mimo), nemotron_v3, granite_thinking, seed_oss, gemma4, kimi_k2, minimax_m2, deepseek_v4, deepseek_v41, plamo3, and mistral with `reasoning_encoding="special_token"`. A token counts only if the tokenizer has a single id for it. On the real DeepSeek-V4 tokenizer the DSML opener is several tokens, so deepseek_v4 does not change in practice. For plamo3 the token is the end-of-turn tag, which is normally a stop token; I expect that to be harmless but did not test it.

**Tradeoffs.**

- No measurable cost. After reasoning ends, `_get_constraint_bounds` returns before any reasoner call. Only a step with an implicit end token runs one extra single-token `validate_tokens` on the CPU. There is no CPU/GPU sync.

**Limitations.**

- A separate bug, similar to #58315, remains. The GLM tool grammar allows the special `<tool_call>` token inside `<arg_value>`. When the model quotes tool-result text that contains it, arguments break (`Write({})`, missing arguments). Many responses this PR recovers now hit that bug. It will be reported separately.
- Legacy (non-`ParserEngine`) parsers such as `k2_horizon` keep the old behavior until they move to `ParserEngine`.
- Under spec decode, the target can still reject a draft and then sample an implicit end token that the grammar rejects. This predates the PR. @yzong-rh plans to file an issue for it.
- Also unchanged: a prompt that already ends with an implicit end token (`continue_final_message`) still starts the grammar after it, and multi-token text markers cannot be expressed as a token-id set.

**Related.** No open PR changes where the grammar starts after reasoning; #36138, #56403, #57718 and #57754 touch nearby paths.

commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`/v1/chat/completions/batch` never tells the engine how to treat reasoning:
`create_batch_chat_completion` hard-codes `reasoning_ended=None` and leaves
`reasoning_parser_kwargs` unset, while `/v1/chat/completions` computes both.

Both fields travel on the request into `EngineCoreRequest` and are consumed by
`StructuredOutputManager._get_reasoner()`, which rebuilds the request-local
reasoning parser from the forwarded `chat_template_kwargs` -- its own comment
says it does so precisely "so the structured-output gate observes the same
template kwargs used by the frontend".

Without them a template-kwarg-driven parser silently falls back to its default.
With `--reasoning-parser kimi_k3` (or `deepseek_v3`) and
`chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": false}` the single-conversation
endpoint builds an engine-side parser with thinking disabled, so
`is_reasoning_end()` answers True on the prompt and the grammar is applied from
the first token. The batch endpoint built the same parser with thinking
*enabled*, `is_reasoning_end()` answered False, and the structured-output gate
never opened: a batch request that asked for `response_format` received
unconstrained output, with no error to show for it.

This is the batch half of the wiring proposed in #42105; the batch endpoint is
still unwired on main.

and the test asserts the two `engine_client.generate()` calls agree on

single-conversation side is not itself `None`, so the comparison cannot pass
vacuously. A final assertion rebuilds the engine-side reasoner exactly the way

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][MoE] Size the permute scratch from its inputs
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Stop predicting the MoE permute scratch capacity from `FusedMoEConfig`; size it from the inputs it actually receives, growing until the workspace manager is locked. This is intended as the root fix behind #55105 (DeepEP v2 + sequence parallelism) and #60423 (PCP), which each patch a different term of the same capacity formula for the `assert n_token <= self.max_num_tokens` failure in the Humming grouped path.

## Claims

- The Humming grouped experts no longer derive a row bound from `max_num_tokens * dp_size * experts_per_token`, so DP, sequence parallelism, PCP, and DeepEP v2's power-of-two receive buckets cannot make the scratch too small.
- The scratch no longer has a hidden-state buffer or dtype, which removes the `hidden_states.dtype == self.hidden_dtype` mismatch on the prequantized (block-FP8 activation) path.
- `CutlassExpertsFp8` and the CUTLASS W4A8 experts get the same behavior. They sized the scratch with `max_num_tokens` and no `dp_size` factor.
- One scratch is shared per `(num_experts, num_local_experts, device)` instead of one per `(capacity, topk, hidden size, dtype)`.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_permute_unpermute.py tests/quantization/test_humming_mxfp4_block_fp8.py tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py -k "permute or humming or cutlass or block_fp8"` (1x B300) | 906 passed (with `tests/kernels/moe/test_cutlass_moe.py` and `-k "permute or humming or cutlass"`) |
| GSM8K, `nvidia/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4`, `--moe-backend humming`, `VLLM_HUMMING_MOE_GEMM_TYPE=grouped_contiguous`, 1x B300, eager (existing `configs/humming/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4-humming.yaml`) | 0.8817 on 1319 questions (threshold 0.86), 0 invalid |
| GSM8K, same model, DP=2 + EP, `allgather_reducescatter`, CUDA graphs, `--max-num-batched-tokens 3000` | 0.8969 on 1319 questions (threshold 0.86), 0 invalid |
| `pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py -k "test_reload_weights and FP8_DYNAMIC"` (1x B300, `VLLM_CUTLASS` FP8 backend, in-place weight reload) | 1 passed, 1 skipped; failed in CI before the shared-scratch fix |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with PCP on 8x H20 (SM90), run by @wangyicong52 (results in #59857) | reported working; #60423 closed in favor of this PR |
| pre-commit on changed files, `mypy-3.12` | passed |

Not validated:

- The DeepEP v2 topology from #55105 is not reproduced here: DeepEP v2 is unavailable on the test machine (NCCL 2.29.7 < 2.30.4). @elvircrn, could you try this branch on your setup?
- The prequantized Humming grouped path (block-FP8 activations before dispatch) was not run with real kernels; in-tree coverage of `HummingGroupedExperts.apply` is mock-based. It is guarded by dtype and shape assertions.

## Details

**Root cause.** `workspace13`/`workspace2` are sized from the actual `M` and grow until `lock_workspace()`. `MoEPermuteScratch` was instead sized up front from config, which requires knowing how many rows every prepare/finalize backend can return in every topology. That bound is a property of the dispatcher, not of the experts, and it has been wrong for PCP, for DeepEP v2 with non-power-of-two capacities, and for CUTLASS with DP.

**Change.**

- `MoEPermuteScratch` holds only index metadata and gains `reserve(expanded_rows)`. It reallocates while the workspace manager is unlocked and raises `Scratch growth is not allowed after locking` afterwards, matching the shared workspace's contract.
- Permuted hidden states come from the caller's workspace. CUTLASS already passed a `workspace2` slice. Humming's prequantized path now writes into `quanted_gate_up_input`, which is allocated with the right shape and dtype and is otherwise unused when w13 quantization is skipped, so this costs no extra memory.
- The index buffers stay a persistent resource rather than moving into `get_simultaneous`: a second `get_simultaneous` call inside `apply()` would alias the live `workspace13`/`workspace2`, and `token_expert_indices` is an `arange` that would otherwise be refilled every call. They are small (seven int32 arrays over the expanded rows plus the sort workspace).

**Tradeoffs and limitations.**

- A runtime shape larger than anything seen during warmup still fails, with the same contract and at the same point as `workspace13`.
- `moe_permute(scratch=...)` without `permuted_hidden_states` now allocates that tensor per call. Both in-tree callers pass a buffer; `benchmark_moe_permute_unpermute.py`'s scratch numbers are not comparable to earlier ones.
- `get_persistent_resource`'s docstring is loosened from "must not resize" to "must not resize once the manager is locked".
- The CUTLASS experts use the same shared scratch as Humming. A scratch owned by the experts instance broke weight reload: the experts are rebuilt after the workspace is locked, so the new scratch was empty and could not grow (caught by `test_reload_weights` in CI build 93385).
- Anything that first reaches a scratch-using path after the lock, without that path having run during warmup, now fails where the old fixed-size scratch would have allocated lazily.

**Relation to open PRs.** Not a duplicate: #55105 and #60423 extend the capacity formula for one topology each and conflict with each other; this removes the formula. The DeepEP v2 handle-capacity change in #55105 (`next_power_of_2(ceil(max_num_tokens / sp_size))`) is independent and still useful. Searches for `MoEPermuteScratch` and `permute scratch workspace` found no other open PR.

commits.pr_title: [Attention] Allow an NVFP4 KV cache on SM90 with fa2
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

[#46963](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46963) reads an NVFP4 KV cache through FlashInfer's fa2 path on SM8x and SM12x. SM90 is left out although it is in the same position: it has no FP4 conversion instructions, so FlashInfer dequantizes NVFP4 there in software as on SM8x (its prefill notes that every pre-SM100 target runs the same generic 1-byte-KV fa2 path), and FlashInfer's FA3 backend rejects an NVFP4 KV cache. This adds SM90 to the architectures that read NVFP4 with fa2.

## Claims

- `--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4` is accepted with FlashInfer on SM90 and takes the writer and fa2 prefill and decode paths that SM8x uses.
- SM90 decode stays on fa2: the existing NVFP4 exclusion keeps it off XQA, whose NVFP4 path FlashInfer limits to SM12x. NVFP4 on SM90 reports single-token decode CUDA graph support, so with speculative decoding the graph mode drops from FULL to PIECEWISE or NONE, depending on the compilation config.
- Nothing changes on other architectures.

## Validation

Not run on SM90: there is no SM90 hardware here. The SM90 path is checked against FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1's source:

- `vec_dtypes.cuh` uses the `cvt ... e2m1x2` instructions only for `__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 1000`; SM8x and SM90 take the same software conversion.
- `is_fa3_backend_supported` returns `False` for a `uint8` (NVFP4) KV cache, so the `"auto"` prefill and decode wrappers vLLM creates resolve to fa2 on SM90.
- `xqa.py` asserts that XQA reads NVFP4 only on SM12x, and vLLM keeps an NVFP4 cache off XQA through `nvfp4_fa2`.

`test_flashinfer_nvfp4_kv_cache_update`, which checks the writer and the data/scale views against FlashInfer's NVFP4 dequantization, now also runs on SM90. On SM80, where nothing changes, `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_flashinfer.py -k nvfp4` gives 4 passed and `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_dcp_spec_reorder.py -k flashinfer` gives 29 passed, 5 skipped, the same as on `main`; with `tests/kernels/attention/test_attention_selector.py` added and `-k "flashinfer or nvfp4"`, 39 passed, 9 skipped.

## Details

`_nvfp4_kv_on_fa2` now includes SM90, so `supports_kv_cache_dtype` accepts `nvfp4` there, the builder and the impl set `nvfp4_fa2`, and queries stay in the model dtype. `supports_combination` also includes SM90, so head size 64 and attention sinks are refused up front as on SM8x and SM12x, and DCP is refused in the builder as there.

FlashInfer turns off split-KV for NVFP4 only on SM12x, where corruption was reported. Its source records an SM90 check (head_dim 128, the asymmetric 512/256 path and a needle swept across split boundaries) in which split-KV on and off agreed to output rounding, so SM90 keeps split-KV as SM8x does. This vLLM integration has not run on SM90.

[#60452](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60452) removes the NVFP4 exclusion from XQA selection so SM12x can decode NVFP4 with XQA. If both land, SM90 has to stay off XQA for NVFP4, so whichever lands second limits both decode selection and `get_cudagraph_support` to SM12x for NVFP4; blocking it only in `forward` would leave the graph support wrong.

On SM90 an FP8 cache uses FA3 prefill and XQA decode while NVFP4 uses fa2 for both; the throughput difference is not measured here.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Close MessageQueue zmq resources via finalizer to avoid exit
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes an intermittent hang where a spawned EngineCore never exits after a startup failure, timing out `tests/v1/shutdown/test_startup_error.py::test_async_llm_startup_error[forward-2-...]` (seen on AMD CI in `Distributed Torchrun + Shutdown`, which runs with `spawn`). Related: #60121, #60141.

### Root cause

Each `MessageQueue` owns a private zmq `Context` and sockets that are never closed explicitly. After a failed `collective_rpc`, the executor's response `MessageQueue` is only reachable through a reference cycle (`FutureWrapper` → exception → traceback → `collective_rpc` / `get_response` frames → `response_mqs`), so it is freed by the cyclic GC.

When the context and its sockets are collected in the same GC pass, CPython clears the context's weak socket references first. pyzmq's `Context.__del__` → `destroy()` then closes nothing, and `term()` blocks forever on the still-open sockets. pyzmq only skips this after its own atexit hook runs, so the hang occurs when GC triggers inside an earlier atexit hook (e.g. `ray.shutdown`, which lazily imports `ray.dag`).

Evidence:
- Captured stacks of real hangs: `term` ← `destroy` ← `Context.__del__` during GC inside `ray.shutdown`.
- Tracing every engine-process zmq context over 46 runs: the response queue's context (`create_from_handle`) was freed by cyclic GC in exactly the 2 runs that hung, and was not freed or was freed by refcount in the 44 that passed.
- A minimal pure-pyzmq repro (context and socket in a cycle, `gc.collect()`) hangs every time, even with `LINGER=0`, and does not hang without the cycle.

## Fix

Register a `weakref.finalize` per `MessageQueue` that holds the context and sockets, closes the sockets with `linger=0`, then terminates the context.
- The context can no longer be collected as garbage, so the deadlocking `Context.__del__` path is unreachable.
- The finalizer only runs once the queue is unreachable, so no other thread can be using its sockets.
- `atexit = False` keeps exit-time behavior unchanged for queues still alive at shutdown.

## Test Plan

- New `test_reader_in_reference_cycle_is_collected_without_blocking` in `tests/distributed/test_shm_broadcast.py`.
- `pytest tests/distributed/test_shm_broadcast.py`
- Loop the startup-error test with `VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn` on MI300X.

## Test Result

- New test fails on main (GC blocks) and passes with this change; full `test_shm_broadcast.py`: 31 passed.
- Startup-error test with spawn on MI300X (TP=2, CPU limited to match CI): **10 hangs in 544 runs before → 0 hangs in 298 runs after** (expected about 5.5 at the baseline rate).
- pre-commit passes.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Honor stop_token_ids on the Responses API
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`/v1/responses` had no `stop_token_ids` field. `OpenAIBaseModel` uses `extra="allow"`, so a client-sent value (`extra_body={"stop_token_ids": [...]}`) was logged as ignored and never reached `SamplingParams`.

This adds the field on `ResponsesRequest` and applies the same client-first `dict.fromkeys` merge that Chat Completions / Completions use when `default_sampling_params` contains `stop_token_ids` (#22519 / #35076).

Serving already calls `to_sampling_params(..., self.default_sampling_params)` (`OpenAIServingResponses` and `/v1/responses/render`).

## Why this is not a duplicate

Searched open PRs for `Responses stop_token_ids`. Nearby work is different:

- #55483 honors `include_stop_str_in_output` after a stop **token id already matched**.
- #35076 / #44009 cover Chat/Completions / Harmony default propagation, not the Responses request schema.
- #48084 (`min_p`), #51152 (`spaces_between_special_tokens`), and #54469 (`thinking_token_budget` server defaults) are other extra sampling fields and are not changed here.

This does **not** change `ModelConfig.get_diff_sampling_param()`. That helper still only forwards `repetition_penalty` / `temperature` / `top_k` / `top_p` / `min_p` / `max_new_tokens`. Extra EOS from a model's `generation_config.json` (including gpt-oss `</call>`) is applied later in the engine via `SamplingParams.update_from_generation_config`, for every API. The hole this PR closes is the Responses request field / extra-body path.

## Test Plan

commits.pr_title: [Spec Decode][Model] Support DFlash2 draft models with GLM-5.3-Flash
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

`incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2` is the block-diffusion (DFlash2) drafter published for `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`. On current `main` the pair cannot be served: `vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2",...}'` fails during startup, and fixing one failure exposes the next. This PR makes the combination start and serve on NVIDIA (8x H100, TP8 + EP), adds unit coverage for the two non-model changes, and reports a throughput sweep against the existing MTP path. No kernels, defaults, or MTP behaviour are changed.

The three blockers on `main` (9d4d9aa5bc), in the order they surface:

| # | Stage | Error on `main` | Root cause |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | draft model load | `RuntimeError: Model does not support EAGLE3 interface` | `Glm5NextForCausalLM` / `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` (the architecture the DFlash2 checkpoint targets) do not declare `SupportsEagle3`, and `Glm5NextModel` is not an `EagleModelMixin`, so the DFlash speculator cannot register its aux hidden-state layers (`target_layer_ids + 1 = [6, 15, 25, 34, 43]`). |
| 2 | KV cache init | `NotImplementedError: Layer language_model.model.layers.3.self_attn.indexer.k_cache: page size is not divisible by the maximum page size and cannot be padded. Padding is only supported for non-MLA attention layers.` | `_get_kv_cache_groups_glm5_next` bails out as soon as a non-MLA attention layer (the draft's sliding-window GQA layers) is present, so the generic page unifier runs on a spec set it cannot unify (MLA 655,360 B, indexer 21,120 B and draft 163,840 B pages at block_size 640). |
| 3 | config | `ValueError: Number of experts in the model must be greater than 0 when expert parallelism is enabled` | `create_draft_parallel_config` copies `enable_expert_parallel` from the MoE target onto the dense drafter (introduced by #55914 for the DeepSeek-V4 MegaMoE drafter). |

### Changes

- **`vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/model.py` (aux hidden-state capture).** `Glm5NextModel` becomes an `EagleModelMixin`; `Glm5NextForCausalLM` and `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` declare `SupportsEagle3`. The tensor handed to the drafter is not `hidden_states + residual`: GLM-5.3-Flash layers run mHC with 4 residual streams and defer each layer's `hc_post` into the next layer's fused post+pre kernel, so at a layer boundary `residual` is the widened `(T, 4 * hidden)` stream (a naive `hidden + residual` fails with `The size of tensor a (8192) must match the size of tensor b (4) at non-singleton dimension 1`) and `hidden_states` alone is the raw layer output. `_aux_hidden_state()` completes the deferred `hc_post` through a dedicated `MHCPostOp` and contracts the streams back to `hidden_size` with `hc_contract`, which is the quantity SGLang's `_prepare_aux_hidden_state` feeds DFlash2. The capture is read-only: the layer loop keeps consuming the original `(hidden_states, residual, post, comb)` tuple. Non-mHC layer boundaries already carry the summed stream in `hidden_states` and are returned as-is. When any aux layer is requested, `forward` returns `(hidden_states, aux_hidden_states)`; otherwise the return type is unchanged.

### Relationship to existing PRs (duplicate check run on 2026-09-15)

Searches: `gh pr list --state open --search "dflash glm"`, `"GLM-5.3 speculative draft"`, `"create_draft_parallel_config"`, `"enable_expert_parallel draft model"`, `gh pr list --state all --search "dflash"`, `gh issue list --search "GLM-5.3-Flash dflash"`.

- #55682 (Leoyzen, open) implements the aux capture with the same semantics (materialize `hc_post`, then `hc_contract`, at the layer boundary) and adds a CPU unit suite for it. It intentionally leaves the KV-cache layout to a companion change (its description notes the draft sliding-window groups still need one); on the configuration tested here (TP8, `--kv-cache-dtype auto`, H100) `main` + an aux-capture-only change still fails at blocker 2. The `model.py` change here is functionally equivalent for GLM-5.3-Flash's mHC boundaries; if #55682 lands first, this PR rebases onto it and drops its `model.py` hunk.
- #55423 (zixi-qi, draft, needs-rebase) covers aux capture plus a KV layout, but with a different layout design: the draft's sliding-window layers are re-blocked to the MLA block size, padded to the MLA page and aliased into the target's MLA slots (no extra bytes per block; `is_eagle_group` follows `use_eagle_block_drop()`; tested with `disable_eagle_block_drop=true`). This PR keeps the draft in a separate region with its native page instead; it is simpler and needs no block-drop override, but it costs KV capacity (numbers below). The two are alternative designs for reviewers to choose between.
- #56933 (hnt2601, opened 2026-09-15) is the same EP-inheritance fix with a different signature (`draft_model_config: ModelConfig | None`). If it merges first, this PR drops the `speculative.py` hunk.
- #55219 (ivanium, draft) removes the GLM-specific layout in favour of the generic packed layout; if that lands, the `kv_cache_utils.py` part of this PR is superseded.
- #54451 (ROCm: glm5next lacks `SupportsEagle3`) is the ROCm counterpart of blocker 1; this PR only touches the NVIDIA model file.

No open PR makes `GLM-5.3-Flash + GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2` start on `main` end to end; this one does, and the parts overlapping with #55682 and #56933 are flagged above for rebasing.

Due to discussion for kv cache allocation,  this PR just submits the main support in advance.

## Previous full supported performance

**Setup.** 8x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (driver 535.154.05), TP8 + EP, torch 2.13.0+cu129, FlashInfer 0.6.18, Python 3.12, vLLM `main` 9d4d9aa5bc + this branch, V2 model runner (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`). Target `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` (fp8 weights, `--kv-cache-dtype auto`, `--max-model-len 131072`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9`, `--no-enable-flashinfer-autotune`, `--tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45 --enable-auto-tool-choice`). Draft `incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2` (5 sliding-window layers, sliding window 2048, block_size 8). Auto-selected attention backends: FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90 (target), FLASH_ATTN (draft).

**Workload.** 16 fixed prompts (code and prose), greedy (`temperature=0`), `max_tokens=512`, `/v1/chat/completions`. Single stream = 4 sequential prompts after 2 warm-ups; concurrency N = N simultaneous requests (prompts cycled). Aggregate output tok/s, per-request median tok/s in parentheses. `k` = `num_speculative_tokens`, "FA" / "FI" = FlashAttention / FlashInfer draft attention, the number in the config column is `--max-num-seqs`.

| Config | Single stream | Conc 8 | Conc 32 | Conc 64 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DFlash2 k=16, FA, 48 | 178.7 | 848.5 (118.3) | 707.3 (23.1) | - |
| DFlash2 k=8, FA, 48 | 202.1 | 987.7 (136.3) | 2652.5 (94.5) | - |
| DFlash2 k=6, FA, 48 | 218.5 | 1064.5 (145.2) | 2844.3 (101.2) | - |
| DFlash2 k=4, FA, 48 | 220.3 | 1051.3 (148.0) | 2751.6 (98.8) | - |
| DFlash2 k=6, FI, 48 | 202.1 | 1021.0 (141.1) | 2578.8 (95.1) | - |
| **DFlash2 k=6, FA, 96** (run 1) | **223.0** | **1074.0 (145.2)** | **2850.7 (103.9)** | - |
| **DFlash2 k=6, FA, 96** (run 2) | **225.5** | - | **2923.6 (106.7)** | **4269.3 (77.5)** |
| MTP k=5, 96 (baseline) | 160.7 | 853.7 (117.3) | 2377.0 (84.0) | 3721.3 (66.7) |

Acceptance, aggregated from every `SpecDecoding metrics` log line of each run:

| Config | Mean acceptance length | Draft acceptance rate | Per-position acceptance |
|---|---|---|---|
| DFlash2 k=16 | 3.63 | 16.5% | 0.75, 0.54, 0.39, 0.28, 0.20, 0.14, 0.10, 0.08, 0.05, 0.04, 0.02, 0.01, 0.006, 0.004, 0.002, 0.001 |
| DFlash2 k=8 | 3.33 | 29.1% | 0.75, 0.53, 0.36, 0.25, 0.18, 0.12, 0.08, 0.06 |
| DFlash2 k=6 | 3.31 | 38.5% | 0.77, 0.55, 0.39, 0.28, 0.19, 0.13 |
| DFlash2 k=4 | 3.00 | 49.9% | 0.78, 0.56, 0.39, 0.27 |
| MTP k=5 | 3.13 | 42.7% | 0.81, 0.57, 0.37, 0.23, 0.15 |

Takeaways:

- `num_speculative_tokens` is the dominant knob. Acceptance decays to ~0 beyond position 8 (the drafter's block_size), so k=16 pays a 17-token verify per step for the same ~3.3-3.6 accepted tokens; going to k=6 raises conc-32 throughput from 707 to 2924 tok/s (4.1x). k=4..6 is the sweet spot on this workload, k=8 is slightly worse.
- Against MTP k=5 at identical settings, DFlash2 k=6 is faster at every concurrency: +40% single stream, +26% at 8, +23% at 32, +15% at 64.
- FlashInfer as the draft attention backend is 7-9% slower than the auto-selected FlashAttention.
- `--max-num-seqs 96` vs 48: +2-3%, no preemption at concurrency 64.

**KV cache capacity (cost of the separate draft region).**

| Config | Available KV memory | KV capacity | Max concurrency at 131072 tokens |
|---|---|---|---|
| MTP k=5 | 23.61 GiB | 1,802,673 tokens | 13.75x |
| DFlash2 k=6 | 23.49 GiB | 1,358,649 tokens | 10.37x |

Per block (block_size 640) the target uses 11 x 655,360 B MLA pages plus 11 x 21,120 B indexer pages (kpool tails aliased into them); the draft adds 5 x 163,840 B pages and its own per-request block demand to the group-aware capacity estimate, hence 24.6% fewer tokens than MTP at the same memory. #55423's slot-aliasing design avoids this at the price of re-blocking the draft to the MLA page; that is the main trade-off between the two PRs. At `--max-num-seqs 96` this still leaves ~14k tokens per sequence.

## Test Plan

```bash
# Unit tests
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py::test_get_kv_cache_config_glm5_with_dflash_draft_group "tests/test_config.py::test_draft_parallel_config_inherits_ep_only_for_moe_drafters" -v

# Lint and types
pre-commit run --files vllm/config/speculative.py vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/model.py vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py tests/test_config.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py

# Serve (8x H100)
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --served-model-name glm-5.3-flash --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel --tool-call-parser glm47 --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --kv-cache-dtype auto --max-num-seqs 96 --max-model-len 131072 --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2","num_speculative_tokens":6}'
# MTP baseline: same command with --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":5}'

# Tool-calling E2E: 8 scenarios against /v1/chat/completions (auto / required / named tool_choice, zero-arg tool, no tools, thinking off, streaming, multi-turn), see Test Result
# Throughput sweep: 16 prompts, greedy, max_tokens=512, single stream + concurrency {8,32} / {32,64}; per-config server relaunch with the speculative-config JSON above
# Accuracy
.venv/bin/python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --max-concurrency 1
```

## Test Result

**Unit tests.** `3 passed` (the kv-cache test and both parametrizations of the config test).

**pre-commit.** All hooks pass on the five changed files, including `mypy-3.10` (the follow-up commit fixes a `dict` invariance error in `_get_kv_cache_groups_glm5_next`).

**Startup.** Each blocker above was hit and cleared in turn on this branch; the final configuration loads the draft (5 layers, `Overriding draft model max model len from 1048576 to 131072`), builds the KV cache (`GPU KV cache size: 1,358,649 tokens`), captures CUDA graphs and serves.

**Tool-calling E2E** against the running DFlash2 server (`--tool-call-parser glm47`, `--reasoning-parser glm45`): 8/8 pass, zero FSM or CUDA errors in the server log. Repeated after each sweep configuration with the same result.

| Scenario | Checks | Result |
|---|---|---|
| auto tool call | `tool_choice=auto`, one `<tool_call>` parsed into `tool_calls`, arguments valid JSON | PASS |
| required tool call | `tool_choice=required` forces a call | PASS |
| named tool call | `tool_choice={"type":"function","function":{"name":...}}` picks the named tool | PASS |
| named zero-argument tool | tool without parameters yields `arguments == "{}"` | PASS |
| no tools, plain chat | no tool schema, ordinary completion, no stray tags | PASS |
| thinking off | `chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": false}` with tools | PASS |
| streaming tool call | `stream=true`, deltas reassemble to a valid call | PASS |
| multi-turn | tool result fed back, second assistant turn answers from it | PASS |

**GSM8K (5-shot, 1319 questions, greedy, `max_tokens=256`, `--max-concurrency 1 --request-timeout-seconds 7200`; the default 600 s timeout acts as a global deadline at concurrency 1 and truncates the run).**

| Server | Accuracy | Invalid responses | Output tokens | Wall time | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Target only (no speculative config), same machine and flags | 0.931 | 0.0% | 121,390 | 1195 s | 101.6 |
| DFlash2 k=6 (this PR) | 0.939 | 0.0% | 123,732 | 607 s | 203.8 |

The two accuracies differ by 0.8 points (about 10 of 1319 questions), inside the run-to-run spread of this greedy-but-nondeterministic stack (see below); output-token counts match within 2%. DFlash2 delivers the same accuracy at 2.0x the single-stream decode speed.

**Greedy output determinism.** Exact token-level lossless verification is not possible on this stack: with `temperature=0` the same server produces different continuations run to run (16 sweep prompts, 512 tokens, sequential, prompt already cached): target-only 0/16 identical across three runs (median common prefix 272-306 characters before the first divergence), DFlash2 k=6 0/16 identical across three runs (median 237-306), and DFlash2 vs target-only 0/16 identical (median 222-237). The run-to-run spread of the target alone is the same size as the DFlash2-vs-target spread, so the divergence comes from the fp8 MoE + EP numerics of the target (near-tie argmax flips), not from the speculative path; the GSM8K parity above (0.919 vs 0.911) is the meaningful losslessness check.

**Pre-existing crash observed while testing, not introduced by this PR (#55626).** Any step that co-schedules a ~600+ token prefill with a speculative verify step, or a burst of a dozen ~630-token prefills, kills the engine with an asynchronous CUDA fault. It reproduces identically with MTP, whose KV layout on this branch is byte-for-byte the `main` layout, so it is a property of the target's FlashInfer SM90 sparse-MLA path with speculative decoding, matching the traceback location and the FlashInfer core dump posted in #55626.

| Run | Speculative config | Load | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | DFlash2 k=6 | `gsm8k_eval.py` unbounded (100 in flight): 12 prefills of 618-645 tokens in one step, 7578 tokens | `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered`, all 8 workers, reproduced 3/3 |
| A' | DFlash2 k=6, `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` | same | fault attributed to FlashInfer `BatchMLAPagedAttentionSM90` in the target's `flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm90.py::forward_mqa` (`Failed to run MLA, error: an illegal memory access was encountered`) |
| B | DFlash2 k=6 | `--max-concurrency 2`: one 661-token prefill + one 7-token verify step | `CUBLAS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED` (sticky error surfacing in the next GEMM) |
| C | MTP k=5 (main layout) | unbounded: 7 prefills, 4518 tokens | `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered` |
| D | MTP k=5 (main layout) | `--max-concurrency 2`: one 637-token prefill + one 6-token verify step | `CUDA error: an illegal instruction was encountered`, surfacing at `flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm90.py:350 _kv_lens_host` (the same frame as in #55626) |

The throughput sweep and the tool-calling E2E never hit it because their concurrent prompts are short (~30 tokens) and their long prompts run one at a time; GSM8K was therefore run at `--max-concurrency 1`. Prefix caching is not involved (`prefix_cache_stats ... hits=0` in every crash dump).

## Known limitations / follow-ups

- #55626 (above) affects every speculative configuration of GLM-5.3-Flash on SM90 and needs a separate fix; the DFlash2 path inherits it.
- The separate draft region costs KV capacity relative to the slot-aliasing design in #55423 (24.6% fewer tokens than MTP at the same memory); the two designs should be reconciled in review.
- Aux hidden states are not all-gathered under sequence parallelism (`compilation_config.pass_config.enable_sp`); the tested configuration runs with compilation mode NONE, where SP is off. Pipeline parallelism is already gated off for GLM-5.3-Flash and was not exercised.
- Tested with greedy sampling for throughput and the default sampling of the tool-calling scripts; `disable_eagle_block_drop` was left at its default.
- Only the NVIDIA model file is changed; the ROCm copy (#54451) is not addressed.

commits.pr_title: [MoE] MXFP4 oracle: add CUTLASS W4A4 backend and BF16 activation fallback
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

First step of #54959 for the packed MXFP4 MoE methods. This PR only touches the MXFP4 oracle; no quant method changes behaviour yet.

**Contract.** The `activation_key` passed to `select_mxfp4_moe_backend` is the activation precision the checkpoint declares (`None` = BF16). Backends that match it are preferred. If none supports the deployment, the oracle falls back to BF16-activation backends and logs a warning, so a W4A4 checkpoint runs as W4A16 on hardware without a W4A4 kernel. Activations are never quantized below what the checkpoint declares.

Previously a non-`None` key was an exact filter, so a W4A4 checkpoint raised on any deployment without a W4A4 kernel (including `--moe-backend marlin`). This matches the MXFP4 linear kernels, where weight-only kernels already accept MXFP4 activation keys as a fallback.

**CUTLASS W4A4 backend.** `CUTLASS_MXFP4_MXFP4` (vLLM's `CutlassExpertsMxfp4`) is added to the oracle: enum, kernel class, scale swizzle in `convert_weight_to_mxfp4_moe_kernel_format`, quant config and 128 round-up. Today that kernel is only reachable through device probes hand-rolled in `CompressedTensorsW4A4Mxfp4MoEMethod` and `INCMxfp4MoEMethod`.

**Behaviour change for existing callers.** Callers that pass no activation key (gpt-oss) and callers of `select_deepseek_v4_mxfp4_moe_backend` (DeepSeek-V4, Kimi-K3) select the same backend as main for every `--moe-backend` value I compared. Callers that already pass a key (online MXFP4, Quark W4A4 and static-FP8 W4A8) change only where main raises:

| Caller | `--moe-backend` | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Online MXFP4 / Quark W4A4 | auto | raises | CUTLASS W4A4 |
| Online MXFP4 / Quark W4A4 | marlin, flashinfer_trtllm, triton_unfused, humming | raises | that backend, BF16 activations |
| Quark W4A8 static FP8 | auto | raises | TRTLLM BF16 |
| Quark W4A8 static FP8 | marlin, flashinfer_trtllm, triton_unfused, humming | raises | that backend, BF16 activations |
| gpt-oss with `quantization_config.moe.activation=mxfp8` | marlin, triton, triton_unfused, humming | raises | that backend, BF16 activations |

Measured on NVIDIA SM103 without `amd-quark`. I have not loaded a model through these newly reachable combinations, and could not measure ROCm. With `amd-quark` installed on CUDA SM100, W4A4 would select CUTLASS ahead of EMULATION.

**Relation to #59460.** The fallback is the default here; #59460 (`VLLM_STRICT_QUANT_SCHEME`) is the opt-in to refuse it. This PR passes BF16 fallback backends their own key, so whichever lands second should pass the checkpoint key through and let `executed_activation_key` report the downgrade, replacing the warning added here.

**Why this is split out.** #55232, #56306 and #56523 each move the CUTLASS swizzle into the oracle and each add a different selection path next to it (an `input_quant` flag, `select_w4a4_mxfp4_moe_backend`, a `candidates=` list). The mechanical part is the same in all three; the selection contract is what differs and what review has stalled on. This PR settles the contract in the existing `activation_key` argument, with no new entrypoint. A follow-up reduces the compressed-tensors and INC methods to weight creation plus oracle delegation.

Not a duplicate: those PRs change the quant methods; this one does not, and is intended as the base they (or the follow-up) build on.

**Follow-up motivation (measured on main, NVIDIA B300).** `CompressedTensorsW4A4Mxfp4MoEMethod` selects `CutlassExpertsMxfp4` with MXFP4 activations for every checkpoint and every `--moe-backend` except `b12x`, including weight-only (A16) checkpoints, and fails on shapes that are not 128-aligned (`shape '[960, 34]' is invalid for input of size 36864`).

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py -k select_mxfp4
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_cutlass_moe.py -k oracle_matches
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py tests/kernels/moe/test_cutlass_moe.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_b12x.py tests/kernels/moe/test_topk_softplus_sqrt.py \
  tests/quantization/test_gfx950_moe.py tests/quantization/test_online.py \
  tests/quantization/test_quark.py tests/quantization/test_auto_round.py \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_mxfp4_kernel_selection.py
pre-commit run; pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual
```

- `test_select_mxfp4_moe_backend_respects_checkpoint_activation` (CPU): exact match wins, BF16 fallback (auto and explicit backend), BF16 checkpoint never quantized.
